newsitem.title: USA: US OPTIONS FOCUS - Market seen shaping up for bounce.
newsitem.headline: US OPTIONS FOCUS - Market seen shaping up for bounce.

text.p: Expirations-related activity aside, U.S. options trading patterns suggest the stock market may be ready to rally, analysts said Thursday.
In addition, a market rally if the Federal Reserve raises interest rates early next week is a distinct possibility.
"I think it's all coming together for something positive," said Robert Rack at Cincinnati-based Investment Research Institute.
He noted that index put implied volatilities and the Chicago Board Options Exchange's (CBOE) volatility index .VIX have reached levels last seen at the July bottom.
By about 1130 CST/1730 GMT, the VIX was up 0.69, or roughly 2.9 percent, at 24.44. It reached 25.36 earlier.

Rack said a short-term moving average on the VIX recently reached its highest level since last July. In addition, Tuesday's close at 24.28 was the highest daily close since a 24.43 close on July 23, 1996.
The market's last major bottom was in July.
Some of this week's pickup in volatility can be linked to the expiration of March S&P 500 futures as well as S&P 500 index and S&P 100 index options later this week.

"You've got a triple witch (expiration), the FOMC (Federal Open Market Committee) meeting hanging over the market, so you're going to have some volatility," Rack said. "But I really think it's going to work its way out to the upside."
Next Tuesday, the FOMC meets amid growing speculation it will increase interest rates.

Fed Chairman Alan Greenspan said Thursday the central bank needed to look beyond current economic conditions because of the time lag that interest rate policy changes have and that ideally it must act pre-emptively to keep inflation low.
The comments helped drive the market to its intraday lows, traders said
By about 1130 CST/1730 GMT, the OEX was off 2.49 at 762.64, above its 758.28 intraday low. The SPX was down 3.94 at 781.83. It had reached a session low of 778.04.
June S&P 500 futures, which had hit 782.50, were down 2.35 at 789.90, well off their session low.

Jerry Hegarty, an analyst at Thomson Financial Services, said in a report that the fact that the OEX had drastically outperformed S&P 500 futures in the first three days of this week was bullish for Thursday and Friday.
